messages:
Alex: quick follow-up — trying to simplify spillback policy for host<->GPU offload. TL;DR: prefer a deterministic eviction order + a single fallback lane instead of complex per-tenant heuristics. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Jordan: curious — deterministic for perf predictability, right? worried about fairness across tenants if we use a single fallback lane.
Alex: yes, perf predictability and easier SLOs. fairness -> we can add soft quotas and gradual backoff rather than strict per-tenant lanes.
Sam: tradeoff is tail latency vs cost. single fallback reduces variance but increases hot-tenant impact. we should quantify — suggest running a simulation over a 2-week trace.
Priya: can we keep allocator ABI unchanged? if the fallback lane is just a reserved host pool, implementation could live in the offload manager, avoiding allocator churn.
Alex: that's the idea — allocator exposes a tiny reserve_hint API: reserve_hint(size, purpose='fallback') so offload manager can prebook without changing core allocation paths. minimal surface.
Jordan: can you sketch reserve_hint? how does it interact with eviction tokens and soft reserves?
Priya: sketch: 
```
// allocator.h
int reserve_hint(size_t bytes, enum hint_purpose); // returns 0 on OK, -ENOSPC if not enough
// offload manager calls reserve_hint before initiating spill to host pool
```
Priya: if reserve_hint fails, offload manager falls back to per-tenant throttling and avoids hard OOM paths. keeps allocator semantics simple.
Sam: also consider telemetry + control loop: hot-tenant fingerprinting -> gradual throttle -> candidate migration to dedicated pool if repeated breaches. we should avoid instantaneous model migration.
Alex: agreed. also need clear eviction ordering heuristics: prefer compactable slabs first, then migratable pages (cheap copy), then forced spill of large contiguous pages. that keeps compaction cheap and minimizes recompute.
evictor-bot: evictor alert — test cluster canary-3 observed ~15% increase in stall during single-lane experiments at 03:14 UTC
Jordan: noted. canary data suggests stalls appear when fallback pool is saturated; we need backpressure signals (queue length, host-pool fill ratio) exposed to request router.
Alex: action items: 1) Sam: run 2-week trace sim + cost/latency curves. 2) Priya: draft reserve_hint API PR and implementation sketch. 3) Jordan: add fallback-pool backpressure metrics and alert thresholds. I'll coordinate rollout plan and canary gating. :thumbsup:
Sam: ack — starting sim today, will post results in ~48h.
Priya: starting API PR, will tag Alex for design review.
Jordan: adding metrics dashboard widgets and a small alert rule.
Alex: cool — if anyone thinks this misses a major failure mode call it out now, otherwise I'll push an RFC follow-up that includes the sim plan and the reserve_hint spec.
